ar1_souls_leakage.note: Nothing in a synthesised ambience bed carries a Morrowind combat mechanic. No roll-to-hit, no dice, no pause, no level scaling is reachable from this subsystem.

ar2_morrowind_leakage.note: No objective marker, bonfire warp, procedural loot or soul-currency purchase is expressed through the ambience layer.

ar3_seam_sterility.justification: The ambience model carries no boundary-crossing interaction. It is driven BY the world (region, position, time of day, weather are written into the driver from _afterStep) and read back only by instruments. Nothing a faction rank, a disposition, a quest resolution or a lore fact does changes what a region sounds like, and nothing a region sounds like changes what any entity does. This is the same finding as CONSUMPTION below, seen from the seam side: the subsystem is a leaf in both directions.

biggest_gap.what: RI-AUD03 §A's 'Level (rel. bed)' band is a claim about EVENTS, and every mechanism that touches it is a per-layer median: gate O3 grades the median of a bed/layer's events, and the corrective trim `event_gain_db` is a single number per layer, while the second gain stage it corrects (`synth.gain_db`, -5..-13) varies PER EVENT. A per-layer trim cannot in principle unbury an event quieter than its layer-mates; it can only move the whole spread. The result is that the round-1 defect this piece exists to close -- declared in band, buried by a second gain stage -- is still present for individual events while the gate reports zero failures: 54 of 413 measured events sit outside §A's band with the tool's own +/-2 dB tolerance, 33 of them buried below the floor, in 11 of 33 bed/layer pairs whose median passes.
biggest_gap.why_it_matters: The buried events are not marginal ones. blackwood/L3/distant_axe renders at -23.1 dB relative to the bed -- 15 dB below §A's floor -- and 'distant axe-strokes' is one of the three sounds that bed's own `brief` field advertises. deep-marshes/L3/marsh_gas_release reaches -30.4 dB. well/L3/stone_shift -16.3, dungeon/L3/block_settle -11.1. From the player's chair those sounds do not exist, which is exactly the state the B2 judge described as 'nothing ever happens in any of them' and exactly the state this round was commissioned to end. Because the gate is green, no future round has a reason to look.
biggest_gap.remedy: Gate O3 on EVERY measured event rather than on the layer median -- the check is already written and falsifiable at tools/audio/critic-w1-22-r2-bands.mjs B1, which goes red on the shipped tree, redder under --sabotage widen, and GREEN under --sabotage centre (every event collapsed onto its layer median), proving its reading is about the spread and not about the level. Then give the trim the same granularity as the stage it corrects: calibrate a per-EVENT gain rather than one `event_gain_db` per layer, since the quantity being corrected varies per event. Both halves are small and neither needs new engine code.
